map.F=G·m₁·m₂/r²=6.674×10⁻¹¹·1·1/1²≈6.67×10⁻: F = G x m1 x m2 / r^2 = 6.674 x 10^-11 x 1 x 1 / 1^2, about 6.67 x 10^-11 N, extremely weak. If instead the Earth and a 1 kg object close to the surface are used, with m2 = 5.97 x 10^24 and r = 6.37 x 10^6, then F is about 9.8 N (that is, the weight of about 1 kg).
map.引力为什么叫平方反比？: Why is gravitation called an inverse-square law?
map.力的大小与距离的平方成反比，距离翻倍则引力减为四分之一，这是天体轨道稳定的核心规: The magnitude of the force is inversely proportional to the square of the distance, so doubling the distance reduces the force to a quarter. This is the core law behind the stability of celestial orbits.
map.G 是什么，为什么这么小？: What is G, and why is it so small?
map.G 是万有引力常数，数值极小说明日常尺度下引力远弱于电磁力，只在天体质量级才显著: G is the gravitational constant. Its extremely small value means that at everyday scales gravity is far weaker than the electromagnetic force and becomes significant only at the mass scale of celestial bodies.
